patterns.usage_note: Gives the speaker's own grounds for saying or doing something, which is why commands and statements of intent prefer it (熱いから触るな); a noun naming a cause takes it directly too (不注意から事故が起こる). Two sibling entries take the other readings: the starting point of a range (九時から) and the party an action comes from (先生から聞いた). A noun or na-adjective needs だ first (休みだから).

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]が待[ま]っているから、急[いそ]いで教室[きょうしつ]へ行[い]こう。
examples.english: The teacher's waiting for us, so let's hurry over to the classroom.

examples.ruby: 危[あぶ]ないから、そこには近[ちか]づかないでください。
examples.english: It's dangerous, so please don't go near there.

examples.ruby: 財布[さいふ]を家[いえ]に忘[わす]れたから、お金[かね]が払[はら]えない。
examples.english: I left my wallet at home, so I can't pay.

patterns.usage_note: Gives the reason as a plain circumstance rather than as the speaker's insistence (熱があるんで、早めに帰ります), which makes it the softer form for excusing yourself or asking to be let off. It is the spoken contraction of ので: say んで, and write ので in email or anything more formal. A noun or na-adjective attaches with な (不在なんで), never だ.

examples.ruby: ちょっと熱[ねつ]があるんで、今日[きょう]は早[はや]めに帰[かえ]ります。
examples.english: I'm running a bit of a fever, so I'll head home early today.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]から出[で]るんで、二十分[にじゅっぷん]ほどで着[つ]きます。
examples.english: I'm leaving now, so I'll be there in about twenty minutes.

examples.ruby: 駅前[えきまえ]の道[みち]が混[こ]んでいるんで、少[すこ]し遅[おく]れます。
examples.english: The road by the station is jammed, so I'll be a little late.

patterns.usage_note: Packages the reason as a state of affairs the speaker was swept along by, so it is the grammar of excuses and self-justification (上司がしつこく催促するもんだから、慌てて送った). The main clause reports what happened, so commands, requests and invitations cannot follow it (×うるさいもんだから静かにしてください); から takes all of those. A noun or na-adjective attaches with な (苦手なもんだから).

examples.ruby: 上司[じょうし]がしつこく催促[さいそく]するもんだから、慌[あわ]てて資料[しりょう]を送[おく]った。
examples.english: My boss kept badgering me about it, so I fired off the documents in a panic.

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の犬[いぬ]が一晩中[ひとばんじゅう]吠[ほ]えるもんだから、苦情[くじょう]を言[い]いに行[い]った。
examples.english: The dog next door barked all night long, so of course I went over to complain.

examples.ruby: 昼[ひる]の行列[ぎょうれつ]がすごいもんだから、ラーメンは諦[あきら]めて帰[かえ]った。
examples.english: The lunchtime line was ridiculous, so I gave up on the ramen and went home.

patterns.usage_note: Lays the reason down as a circumstance and lets the sentence trail off, which makes it the standard opener of an apology or excuse (急な用事が入ったもんで、失礼いたします). It is milder than もんだから, which pushes the excuse at the listener, and it shares the family's block on commands, requests and invitations in the main clause. A noun or na-adjective attaches with な (急用なもんで).

examples.ruby: 毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]に家[いえ]を出[で]るもんで、夜[よる]は早[はや]く寝[ね]ています。
examples.english: I leave the house at six every morning, you see, so I turn in early.

examples.ruby: 電波[でんぱ]がここだけ弱[よわ]いもんで、声[こえ]が途切[とぎ]れて申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません。
examples.english: The signal is poor just here, so I'm sorry if I keep cutting out.

examples.ruby: この時期[じき]はどうしても忙[いそが]しくなるもんで、返事[へんじ]が遅[おそ]くなりました。
examples.english: This time of year always gets hectic, so I'm sorry to be slow replying.

patterns.usage_note: Hands over a personal reason or excuse at the end of a sentence, with a note of complaint or 甘え, usually answering a preceding だって or なんで (だって眠いんだもん). The same shape carries two other senses: stating a social norm as advice (早く寝るもんだ) and exclaiming over something taken as a truth (月日が経つのは早いもんだ). It follows plain forms directly, and a noun needs だ first (まだ子供だもん); もん is blunter than もの.

examples.ruby: だって、私[わたし]よりあの子[こ]のほうが上手[じょうず]にできるもん。
examples.english: But she's better at it than I am!

examples.ruby: 今[いま]さらそんなこと言[い]われても困[こま]るもん。
examples.english: You can't spring that on me now; it just leaves me stuck.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]だって約束[やくそく]はちゃんと守[まも]るもん。
examples.english: I keep my promises too, you know.
